challenges.name: errors-wrapping-quiz
challenges.title: Predict it: %v, %w, errors.Is and errors.As
challenges.description: Decide what a wrapped error prints and matches, then which ways of inspecting an error look through the wrappers.

questions.explanation: %v formats ErrNotFound as text, so the message is lookup SP-9999: parcel not found - exactly the same text that %w would give. But %v only copies the text into a new error: the new error does not keep ErrNotFound inside it, so errors.Is finds nothing to unwrap and returns false. With %w, fmt.Errorf returns an error that wraps ErrNotFound, and errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound) is true. Two errors with the same message are not the same error; errors.Is compares error values, not strings.

options.text: lookup SP-9999: parcel not found, then true
lookup SP-9999: parcel not found, then false
lookup SP-9999: &errors.errorString{s:"parcel not found"}, then false
It does not compile: %v cannot format an error

questions.question: ErrNotFound is a sentinel error made with errors.New, and *ValidationError is an error type (its Error method has a pointer receiver). Which statements are true? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: errors.Is follows the whole chain of %w wrappers, so an ErrNotFound wrapped twice is still found. == compares the outermost error only: fmt.Errorf("lookup: %w", ErrNotFound) is a new *fmt.wrapError value, not ErrNotFound. A type assertion, like ==, only looks at the outermost error, so err.(*ValidationError) fails on a wrapped one; errors.As(err, &ve) walks the chain (and the errors inside errors.Join) and sets ve to the first *ValidationError it finds. Returning a nil *ValidationError from a function whose result type is error gives an error interface that holds a type and a nil pointer, and that interface is not nil: err == nil is false. Return a literal nil instead.

options.text: errors.Is(fmt.Errorf("GET: %w", fmt.Errorf("lookup: %w", ErrNotFound)), ErrNotFound) is true
After err := fmt.Errorf("lookup: %w", ErrNotFound), err == ErrNotFound is true
A type assertion err.(*ValidationError) succeeds when the *ValidationError was wrapped with %w
With var ve *ValidationError, errors.As(err, &ve) finds a *ValidationError through %w wrappers and inside errors.Join
A function with result type error that returns a *ValidationError variable holding nil returns an error that is == nil

challenges.name: fix-trackd-status-codes
challenges.title: Fix trackd's error handling so every request gets the right status code
challenges.description: trackd, Saigon Parcel's tracking API, turns the error a request ends with into an HTTP status code: 400 for an invalid request (a *ValidationError anywhere in the chain), 404 for an unknown parcel (ErrNotFound), 409 for rescheduling a parcel that is already delivered (ErrConflict), 500 for anything else. After a refactor it answers 500 for almost everything: for parcels that exist, for unknown parcels and for invalid ids. Fix how the errors are returned, wrapped and compared so every request gets its status code. Keep the error message texts. The test runner sends get and reschedule requests and prints the status code and the result or the error for each one.

tests.name: Parcels that exist answer 200
tests.expected:
get SP-2001: 200 SP-2001 out_for_delivery
get SP-2002: 200 SP-2002 delivered

tests.name: An unknown parcel answers 404
tests.expected:
get SP-9999: 404 lookup SP-9999: parcel not found
get SP-2003: 200 SP-2003 at_hub

tests.name: Invalid ids answer 400
tests.expected:
get 2001: 400 lookup 2001: id: must start with SP-
get SP-20011: 400 lookup SP-20011: id: must be SP- and 4 digits

tests.name: Reschedule: 200 for a parcel at the hub, 409 for a delivered one
tests.input:
reschedule SP-2003 sat
get SP-2003
reschedule SP-2002 mon
tests.expected:
reschedule SP-2003 sat: 200 SP-2003 at_hub, day sat
get SP-2003: 200 SP-2003 at_hub, day sat
reschedule SP-2002 mon: 409 reschedule SP-2002: parcel already delivered

tests.name: Reschedule errors from every layer: unknown parcel, bad day, bad id
tests.input:
reschedule SP-9999 mon
reschedule SP-2001 sunday
reschedule SP-01 mon
tests.expected:
reschedule SP-9999 mon: 404 reschedule: lookup SP-9999: parcel not found
reschedule SP-2001 sunday: 400 reschedule SP-2001: day: must be one of mon tue wed thu fri sat
reschedule SP-01 mon: 400 reschedule: lookup SP-01: id: must be SP- and 4 digits

tests.name: A mixed sequence of requests
tests.input:
get SP-2002
reschedule SP-2001 fri
get SP-2001

tests.expected:

reschedule SP-2001 fri: 200 SP-2001 out_for_delivery, day fri
get SP-2001: 200 SP-2001 out_for_delivery, day fri
get sp-2001: 400 lookup sp-2001: id: must start with SP-
reschedule SP-2002 sat: 409 reschedule SP-2002: parcel already delivered
